Representing Central America at the 2013 Dragon Duel World Championship is 12-year-old Marco Jossue Ruiz Campos from Heredia, Costa Rica! He was playing a Dragon Ruler Deck. In 2nd place was Juan Carlos Coronel Contreras, an 11-year-old from Jalisco, Mexico, who was playing a Spellbook Deck. In 3rd was Angel Arturo Borja Aquino, another 11-year-old from Mexico D.F., playing a Dragon Ruler Deck, and in 4th place was Daniel Isai Coronel Contreras, younger brother of Juan Carlos, a 10-year-old from Jalisco, Mexico. Congratulations to all, and we’ll see Marco in Vegas!

This weekend sees the continuation of the Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME World Championship Qualifiers. We’re in Monterrey, Mexico at the Cintermex to determine who will represent Central America at the 2013 World Championship Tournament next month in Las Vegas, Nevada. Don’t forget – the World Championship will have plenty of Public Events that anyone can participate in, in addition to some fun Yu-Gi-Oh! themed games. So not only can you cheer on your favorite Duelist, but you can also join in some fun!

But back to this weekend. We’ve got a total of 378 Duelists for the Main Event and here are the country breakdowns: 1 Duelist from the Dominican Republic, 1 from El Salvador, 1 from Honduras, 1 from Jamaica, 2 from Trinidad, 2 from Guatemala, 8 from Panama, and 11 from Costa Rica. The remaining Duelists are from Mexico. Welcome everyone, Duel hard but have fun!
We had some visa issues for some of our young Duelists hoping to compete today, so our Dragon Duel WCQ is a little small.
We have 4 Duelists from Mexico, DF, who normally play at Monster Sprim, the organizer for today. In addition, we have one from Guatemala and 2 from Costa Rica.

Some of the notable faces from today´s WCQ are the WCQ – National Champions from the Central American countries. Hoping to top their National status to Continental status are Alejandro Rafael Canas Batres from Guatemala, Yorquin Medina Buten from the Dominican Republic, Rolando Alberto Gordon Bustamante from Panama, Hector Leonel Ortega from Honduras,
from El Salvador, Shawn Kenroy Russell from Jamaica, Leobardo Sanchez Gonzalez from Mexico and Tomas Jimenez Acosta from Costa Rica.
Some other notables are the YCS Champions: Angel Zayren Flores Covarrubias, the Guatemalan YCS Champion and Jorge Luis Campos Valverde, the Costa Rican YCS Champion.
DeObaldia Soza from Panama is here, as is the 2012 Central American Champion, Alvaro Manuel Gonzalez Orea from Mexico.

On the Dragon Duel side, the Guatemalan National Champion, Diego Alejandro Diaz Herrarte, and the Mexican Dragon Duel Champion, Angel Aarturo Borja Aquino, are competing to represent Central America at the Dragon Duel World Championship.
